gaps.sentence: ___ his leg was strapped up, the captain insisted on playing.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' intensifies the concession before a full clause.

gaps.sentence: ___ the investors backed the plan enthusiastically, but they withdrew after the scandal.
gaps.hint: at the start, not the end
gaps.explanation: 'Initially' contrasts the early support with the later withdrawal.

gaps.sentence: The lecture was dull; ___, the students stayed awake out of politeness.
___ she was utterly exhausted, she stayed to help clear up.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a known fact: she was exhausted and still stayed.

gaps.sentence: Please complete the form in block capitals ___ it can be read easily.
gaps.explanation: 'So that' introduces a clause with subject and modal; so as to/in order to need an infinitive.

gaps.sentence: The negotiations dragged on for months, but they ___ collapsed.
gaps.explanation: 'Eventually' signals the outcome after much delay.

gaps.sentence: He is far from lazy; ___, he trains six hours a day.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' rejects the description and states the reverse, more strongly.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.
